summary: Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at Tübingen, Hamburg, Bonn, Princeton, Kiel (PhD), and Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg in 1970 and served as a professor at Saarland University from 1974 to 1998.

Linguist Kuno Meyer studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1883). He held posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919), where he succeeded Heinrich Zimmer in 1911.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya earned her PhD at Jadavpur University under Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, having also studied under Prabal Kumar Sen. She held an attested post at Rabindra Bharati University in 2009.
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Patrul Rinpoche (~1880–1887). He taught students including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro (1952–2014) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

Kurt A. Behrendt, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD from UCLA (~1991–1997). At the Metropolitan Museum of Art, he served as Assistant Curator (~2005–2014) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2014).
Kurt Andrew Johnson, who works in Indology and other fields, completed his PhD at the University of York by 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber studied at the Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1913–1917). Working in philosophy and other fields, he served at the University of Munich as an außerordentlicher Professor (1926) and Professor (1938).

Kurt Tropper specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Vienna in 2001 under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Schaeffer earned degrees from Lewis & Clark, Evergreen State, Washington, and Harvard (PhD, 2000). He held faculty posts at the University of Alabama (2000–2004) and joined the University of Virginia in 2005.
Kurunegoda Piyatissa (1928–2008) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was head of the New York Buddhist Vihara, where his posts are attested in 1998 and 2009.

Kwangsoo Park, a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, completed an MA at the University of Iowa and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

Kyo Kano studied Indology and philosophy at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna. Kano served as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and as an associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).

Buddhist studies scholar Kyojun Shimizutani studied at Tendai Sect University and Taisho University. He held professorships at Tendai Sect University (1919) and Taisho University (1926–1945), and served as head priest of Senso-ji (~1952–1979).

After studying at the University of Tokyo, Buddhist and Indology scholar Kyoko Fujii held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1998–2007) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2007–2019), later directing the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026).
Kyoko Tokuno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who taught Douglas Ober. She held academic posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington (attested 2017 as professor).

Kyokuga Saeki (1828–1891) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Reiga and Gen'yū. He served as the 143rd elder of Sennyu-ji and taught students including Shundo Sugihara.

Kyosho Hayashima (1914–1999) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held teaching posts at Yokohama City University (1962), Toyo University (1962), and the University of Tokyo (1980), and his students included Shinjo Kawasaki and Fumihiko Sueki.
Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. Around 1974, he served as an associate professor at Musashino University.
